clue.text: Church recently admitting single Bishop's chaste

parts.note: CE is the Church of England

indicators.note: admitting means letting something in, so one word takes others inside it

parts.note: recently means late, as in 'the late king'
single is one, the Roman numeral I
B is the chess abbreviation for bishop

explanation.surface: A churchman notes that a bishop who has lately taken in a single person remains chaste.
explanation.walkthrough: 'admitting' signals the container; 'recently' as LATE is the 'late' of 'the late king'. The 's of Bishop's is just a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone celibate abstains from sexual relations, which is what chaste describes.

clue.text: The old vinyl record 'Shout'

parts.note: ye is the old way of writing 'the'
an LP is a long-playing vinyl record

explanation.surface: An old vinyl single titled 'Shout'.
explanation.definitionFit: A yelp is a short sharp cry, a kind of shout.

clue.text: Degeneration on 'ampstead 'eath?

parts.note: Hampstead Heath is Cockney rhyming slang for teeth, so this is decay affecting the teeth

explanation.surface: Something going to ruin on a London common, spoken in Cockney.
explanation.walkthrough: Hampstead Heath is a park in north London; in Cockney rhyming slang it means teeth, and the dropped Hs show the Cockney voice.
explanation.definitionFit: Caries is the medical term for tooth decay, a degeneration of the teeth.

clue.text: Group practised holding jam turned up…

indicators.note: holding means containing, so one word wraps round another

parts.note: practised means skilled or able

indicators.note: turned up in a down clue means the word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: a jam is a mess, a tight spot

explanation.surface: A skilled band holding a jam session that has just shown up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turned up' gives SSEM in a down clue, and 'holding' wraps the practised word round it; 'Group' is the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To assemble is to gather together, to group, both verbs.

clue.text: …'Asia' perhaps, including start of great group

indicators.note: including means taking in, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: Asia is an example of a continent

indicators.note: start of means only the first letter of the word great is used

explanation.surface: Asia, perhaps, contains the beginnings of a great group.
explanation.walkthrough: 'including' puts G, the first letter of 'great', inside CONTINENT. The dots link it to the previous clue's surface.
explanation.definitionFit: A contingent is a group of people forming part of a larger body.

clue.text: Knight, brave man's protecting birds

indicators.note: protecting means surrounding, so one piece wraps round the other

parts.note: a brave man is a hero, with the possessive S kept
N is the chess notation for knight

explanation.surface: A knight and a brave man look after some birds.
explanation.walkthrough: 'protecting' puts N inside HERO'S.
explanation.definitionFit: Herons are long-legged wading birds.

clue.text: Philosopher with jug held noxious liquid

indicators.note: held means the second piece is contained by the first

parts.note: a sage is a wise man or philosopher
a ewer is a large jug

explanation.surface: A thinker holds a jug of something foul.
explanation.walkthrough: 'held' signals the container: the jug sits inside the philosopher.
explanation.definitionFit: Sewerage is the waste water carried in sewers, unpleasant liquid.

clue.text: Examination ends on fine ancient shroud

indicators.note: ends means only the first and last letters of the word examination are taken

parts.note: F is the abbreviation for fine, as on pencils
ancient means old

explanation.surface: The final part of an examination about an old burial cloth.
explanation.definitionFit: To enfold is to wrap up or envelop, as a shroud does to a body.

clue.text: Start to sing shanty, it helps the stoker

indicators.note: start to means only the first letter of the word sing

parts.note: a shanty is a crude hut, a hovel

explanation.surface: Someone begins a sea shanty while stoking a ship's boiler.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shanty' looks like the sailors' song; it is the hut.
explanation.definitionFit: A stoker uses a shovel to feed coal into a furnace.

clue.text: Impediment getting mouth around sibilant?

indicators.note: around means the first piece surrounds the second

parts.note: lip is mouth in the sense of cheek or impudence, and also part of the mouth
S is the classic sibilant, hissing sound

explanation.surface: A speech defect makes the mouth twist round a hissing sound.
explanation.walkthrough: 'around' puts S inside LIP.
explanation.definitionFit: A lisp is a speech impediment affecting S sounds.

clue.text: Pitch is left in clinical condition

indicators.note: in means the second piece is placed inside the first

parts.note: an infection is a medical condition

explanation.surface: A tone of voice is left behind in a hospital diagnosis.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pitch' could be a field or tar; here it is tone of voice.
explanation.definitionFit: An inflection is a change in the pitch or tone of the voice.

clue.text: Endless palaver engulfing a second star

indicators.note: engulfing means swallowing up, so one piece wraps round others
endless means the final letter of the word is dropped

parts.note: palaver means a fuss, a lot of bother
a mo is a moment, a second

explanation.surface: A drawn-out fuss swallows a star's moment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Endless' leaves FUS, and 'engulfing' wraps it round the other pieces; star is an adjective here.
explanation.definitionFit: Star used as an adjective means celebrated or leading, much like famous.

clue.text: Shot scene with a plot twist

indicators.note: a plot twist rearranges events, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A film scene shot with a plot twist.
explanation.walkthrough: 'twist' rearranges SCENE, A and PLOT. 'Shot' is the fabric sense, as in shot silk.
explanation.definitionFit: Shot silk shimmers with changing colours, which is what opalescent describes.

clue.text: Foreign national, the Parisian curses English

parts.note: le is French for 'the'
banes are curses or plagues

explanation.surface: A Frenchman curses the English.
explanation.definitionFit: A Lebanese person is a citizen of Lebanon, a foreigner from a British view.

clue.text: Please turn over and go on

indicators.note: turn over means the letters are turned about into a new order

explanation.surface: Asking someone politely to turn the page and carry on.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turn over' rearranges PLEASE.
explanation.definitionFit: When time elapses it passes, or goes on.

clue.text: Stand still getting beat up in arena

indicators.note: in means one piece is placed inside the other

parts.note: a stage is an arena of activity

indicators.note: up in a down clue means the word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: to tan is to beat, as in 'tan his hide'

explanation.surface: A fighter stands motionless after a beating in the ring.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' gives NAT in a down clue, and 'in' puts it in the arena; 'beat' is to tan a hide.
explanation.definitionFit: To stagnate is to stop moving or developing, to stand still.

clue.text: Small woman about to get tough

parts.note: Eve is the first woman in the Bible
re means about or concerning

explanation.surface: A petite woman is about to become hard.
explanation.definitionFit: Severe means harsh or stern, which is tough.

clue.text: Denounce former wife before end of divorce case

parts.note: an ex is a former wife

indicators.note: end of means only the last letter of the word divorce is used

parts.note: a crate is a packing case

explanation.surface: Someone condemns their ex ahead of the final divorce hearing.
explanation.definitionFit: To execrate is to curse or denounce bitterly.

clue.text: Emblem of French depravity

parts.note: de is French for 'of'
vice is depravity or wickedness

explanation.surface: A symbol of French moral corruption.
explanation.definitionFit: A device is a heraldic emblem or motto.

clue.text: Reporting finished in pen

indicators.note: in means one piece is placed inside the other

parts.note: a pen is an enclosure, a cage
finished means over

explanation.surface: A journalist's piece is done, written up in pen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' signals the container; 'pen' is the enclosure, not the writing tool.
explanation.definitionFit: Coverage is the reporting of news on a subject.

clue.text: Too old really to accept Liberal

indicators.note: to accept means taking something in, so one piece goes inside

parts.note: really means very

explanation.surface: Someone is far too old to welcome a Liberal politician.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to accept' puts L inside VERY, after O.
explanation.definitionFit: Overly means excessively, the same as too in 'too keen'.

clue.text: Almost go out to see 'Midnight Express'

parts.note: read as mid-night, the letter in the middle of the word night
to utter is to express in words

explanation.surface: Nearly going out to watch the film 'Midnight Express'.
explanation.definitionFit: A candle gutters when its flame flickers and nearly goes out.

clue.text: Poor part of town, hard, within reach

indicators.note: within means the second piece sits inside the first

parts.note: to reach a place is to get to it
H is the abbreviation for hard, as on pencils

explanation.surface: A deprived district is hard to reach.
explanation.walkthrough: 'within' puts H inside GET TO.
explanation.definitionFit: A ghetto is a deprived, segregated area of a city.

clue.text: Commercial centre with mail shot

indicators.note: shot means wrecked or broken, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A business hub with a mailshot campaign.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shot' rearranges CENTRE and MAIL; 'mail shot' reads as a marketing letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Mercantile means relating to trade or merchants, i.e. commercial.

clue.text: Blast desperate character embracing right

indicators.note: embracing means hugging, so one piece wraps round another

parts.note: Desperate Dan is a cowboy in the British comic The Dandy

explanation.surface: Curse a desperado hugging the right.
explanation.walkthrough: Desperate Dan is a strongman from the long-running British children's comic The Dandy. 'embracing' puts R inside DAN.
explanation.definitionFit: Darn is a mild exclamation of annoyance, like blast.

clue.text: Tory leader expected to lead twosome

indicators.note: to lead means coming before, so this piece sits first

parts.note: due means expected, as in 'due tomorrow'

indicators.note: leader means only the first letter of the word Tory

explanation.surface: The Conservative leader is expected to head a partnership.
explanation.definitionFit: A duet is a piece performed by two, a pair.

clue.text: Mercury, say, showing level temperature

parts.note: a plane is a flat, level surface

explanation.surface: A thermometer's mercury showing a steady temperature.
explanation.walkthrough: Mercury reads as the liquid in a thermometer; it is the planet.
explanation.definitionFit: Mercury is an example of a planet, the one nearest the Sun.

clue.text: 'Cry wolf' put in appearance

indicators.note: put in means one piece is inserted into the other

parts.note: an entry is an appearance, such as an actor's entrance
to wolf food is to eat it greedily

explanation.surface: A shout of 'Wolf!' turns up on stage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cry wolf' looks like a set phrase; 'Cry' alone is the definition, and 'put in' signals the container with wolf meaning eat greedily.
explanation.definitionFit: An entreaty is an earnest plea, a cry for help.
